title: Surgical hotpatch branching and backport policy for LTS and rolling channels
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Purpose: Define a surgical hotpatch and backport policy that minimizes blast radius while enabling rapid corrective releases across LTS and rolling channels. This ticket codifies severity criteria, patch-branch naming, automated backport helpers, gating checks, and rollback sequencing tied to rollout gates and upgrade tooling.

Scope: Applies to runtime, serving orchestration, and console components for production-hosted and Dedicated deployments. Excludes non-production test artifacts.

Severity classification (operational definitions):
- Sev0 (Critical): Complete service outage impacting all customers, data corruption, or operator ability to safely roll back. Target: 1h mitigation ETA, emergency branch.
- Sev1 (High): Significant degradation for >=5% of requests or major feature break affecting customers with SLAs. Target: 4h mitigation ETA, surgical hotpatch recommended.
- Sev2 (Medium): Functional regression with limited impact or workaround; schedule patch in next minor/patch cycle.
- Sev3 (Low): Cosmetic or non-production impact; tracked but not hotpatched.

Patch branch naming and branching model:
- Naming convention: patch/<component>/<semver>-hotfix/ENG-<id>/<short-desc> (example: patch/runtime/2.0.1-hotfix/ENG-94721/kv-cache-oom).
- Create patch branch from the exact commit of the release tag (not from main). For LTS branches use the maintained branch (eg. release/2.0.x).
- Single purpose: branches must contain only the minimal set of commits required to fix the issue. Cross-cutting changes must be deferred.

Backport policy and matrix:
- Backport when: fix is present in a newer branch and the older branch is active LTS or used by customers and the fix is not purely a feature.
- Matrix: map active branches to supported commits and owners; maintain a BACKPORT.md in the release repo with mapping.
- Tools: provide a backport CLI (upgrade-manager backport --source <commit> --targets <branch-list>) that creates draft PRs with cherry-picks, conflict markers, and test labels.

Gating checks before cut: mandatory CI checks for any hotpatch PR:
- Unit + integration smoke suite (fast subset)
- Binary size and dependency audit scan
- Migration/Schema lints (if applicable)
- Safety check: automated canary plan generated with rollout gates (canary %, error-budget threshold, latency delta threshold).
- Security: SCA and policy scan (required if security_review_required=true).

Rollout gates and staged rollouts:
- Default canary: 1% for 15 minutes, then 5% for 30 minutes, then 25% for 1 hour before full 100%. Gates evaluate error rate, p99 latency, and business metrics (customer-facing errors).
- Automatic rollback trigger: if error-rate increases by >250% over baseline or p99 latency regresses >2x, rollback to previous patch is initiated automatically via routing policy.
- Manual override: on-call Release Engineer can override with explicit reason in PR and incident log.

Rollback sequencing and stateful considerations:
- Stateless services: rollback is via routing change to previous image and invalidating caches where needed.
- Stateful changes (schema migrations, KV format changes): include reversible migration plan. If migration is not reversible, block hotpatch and prefer canaryed forward-only rollout with increased monitoring and customer notifications.
- Post-rollback validation: smoke runbook to verify consumer-facing endpoints, ingestion pipelines, and metrics reconciliations.

Automation and integration with upgrade tooling: 
- upgrade-manager will: create branch, run backport helper, stage draft PRs, run fast CI, create canary rollout plan in Console, and attach canary dashboards.
- GitHub Actions: workflow hotpatch.yaml invoked by label hotpatch/start creates the patch branch and assigns reviewers from the RELEASE_ON_CALL rotation.

Operational runbook snippets (high level):
- Emergency hotpatch workflow: triage -> assign SEV owner -> produce minimal fix -> run backport helper -> open hotpatch PR -> run mandatory CI -> approve -> cut patch release -> monitor canary -> promote.
- Rollback workflow: detect -> evaluate impact -> if automated trigger fires or SEV owner approves, initiate rollback via Console route revert -> POST-rollback validation -> postmortem.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented naming convention and backport matrix checked into release repo.
- Backport CLI prototype that can open draft PRs for at least two target branches.
- CI gating checklist implemented in hotpatch workflow.
- Canary plan templates in Console and automation to attach dashboards.
- Runbook steps added to incident documentation and linked from on-call rotation.

Non-goals: major refactors bundled into hotpatch branches, experimental features, or backward-incompatible migrations without explicit migration toggles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) BACKPORT.md added to release repo and referenced in PR template. 2) backport CLI can create draft PRs for release/2.0.x and release/1.9.x. 3) hotpatch GH workflow enforces fast CI and security scan. 4) canary templates show expected metrics and thresholds. 5) at least one simulated rollback executed in staging using the new flow.

notes: Emphasis on minimal diffs for patch branches and automating the tedious cherry-pick/backport steps to reduce human error. Will coordinate with Console and Upgrade teams for rollout templating.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Docs + naming convention + PR template (2 weeks). Phase 2: backport CLI & GH Action (3 weeks). Phase 3: Console canary templates & automation (2 weeks). Phase 4: Runbook drills and staging rollback test (1 week).
